ratings_why.fun: Every recruit phase is a move-then-buff puzzle, and hanging Climbers on another tribe's engine gives combos the designer didn't list; a few plain cards (Ivy Bush, Hazel Wand) keep it from an 8.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because it inverts buffing itself: Climbers can't be buffed, only copy their host, so spells go dead, other tribes' engines become your growth, and the tribe lives as a parasite on whatever the lobby gives it.

verdict_why: Nothing is broken or unreadable; the remaining notes are taste ideas that would make it different, not better.

points.text: Viscum with Kissing Bough rewards many small hosts, pulling against the one-hub Grand Oak build; that tension is the tribe's best late decision, so keep both.
Ruin Ivy turns Harvest Supper and stray neutral buffs into hub gains every Climber copies; consider one more card that rewards this redirect so it can be a build, not just a fix for dead spells.
Ivy Bush is a vanilla Hold 2; a small trigger when a Climber is dragged onto it would make the re-hanging puzzle pay at Tier 2.

Cousin Dodder riding the enemy's biggest unit is a great trick, but his own fall payoff (+1/+1 to one host) is tiny next to Old Man's Beard; a fight buff to all hosts would tie him into the fall build harder.

standouts.why: Ruin Ivy breaks the tribe's own rule in a way that creates combos with every tribe bonus and stray buff.
The Hon. Viscum Highbough turns every host into a shared well, so board layout becomes a network puzzle.
Lady Hedera rewards hopping across other tribes' units each turn, the social-climber theme as a real decision.

weakest.why: Ivy Bush is a plain socket with no decision of its own.
Hazel Wand grows a little Health and does little else.
Honeysuckle Flatterer is free gold once you have one big hub; the condition rarely bites.

flags.note: Viscum with Kissing Bough gives each Climber about one packet per host per turn, which grows with hosts times Climbers.
Ruin Ivy plus Viscum concentrates every tribe bonus into hosts that all Climbers copy; worth a sim with Harvest Supper.
Golden Grand Oak with Hop Bine on another tribe's scaler is the designer's own runaway risk.
